Descriptions.onelaunch: OneLaunch modifies your default web browser, replaces your taskbar search bar, and consumes continuous background CPU resources.
Descriptions.wavebrowser: Wave Browser is a repackaged browser known to bundle intrusive search modifiers, hijack default file associations, and push unauthorized popups.
Descriptions.driverone: DriverOne is an unverified utility known to flag false system errors and demand recurring credit card subscriptions to 'repair' drivers.
Descriptions.driverfix: DriverFix is an aggressive driver updater known to cause device driver instability and blue screen boot failures.
Descriptions.driversupport: DriverSupport is an unverified utility that displays exaggerated driver error alerts to solicit paid subscriptions.
Descriptions.driverbooster: Driver Booster frequently bundles third-party toolbars and can install untested generic drivers that cause system instability.
Descriptions.drivereasy: Driver Easy aggressively prompts users to upgrade to paid subscriptions for basic driver installations.
Descriptions.segurazo: Segurazo / Santivirus hooks deeply into system services, resists standard uninstallation, and severely slows system responsiveness.
Descriptions.restoro: Restoro is an unverified PC optimizer tool that flags phantom registry errors and displays aggressive payment prompts.
Descriptions.outbyte: Outbyte is an aggressive system cleaner known to flag harmless cache files as critical security warnings.
Descriptions.bytefence: ByteFence bundles with freeware downloaders, alters default browser search engines, and displays nag popups.
Descriptions.totalav: TotalAV frequently installs as a bundled trial via deceptive web ads and generates alarmist popups to push high-cost renewals.
Descriptions.systemmechanic: System Mechanic runs background tasks that often conflict with native Windows Defender and maintenance services.
Descriptions.advancedsystemcare: Advanced SystemCare installs persistent background update daemons that degrade system startup speed.
Descriptions.DefaultFallback: This software is classified by computer repair technicians as a Potentially Unwanted Program (PUP) that commonly injects background processes, modifies browser configurations, displays false error alerts, or degrades computer responsiveness.
